screen1-a1.glyph: red and yellow striped flag with a numeral beside it
screen1-a1.description: flag picture with a count beside it, first item of the top bar
screen1-a1.visible_text: none that names the purpose; a Spanish-style flag glyph and the numeral "1"
screen1-a1.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc/talkback "Learning Spanish" — told me to expect a course/language control; not used in the verdict
screen1-a1.convention_relied_on: a national flag in an app's top bar is an established language/region-selector convention — my reading, confidence medium; the numeral beside it is not explained
screen1-a1.initial_rationale: no words, but a flag is a widely used convention for 'language / course' and the context is a language-learning path; common-icon exemption pending the behavioural test

test_cases.confirms_if: it opens something unrelated to language or course
test_cases.observed_result: a panel dropped down from the top bar showing the current course tile ('Spanish'), a '+ Course' tile, a score card and a 'New Courses' row; the panel also re-opened by itself several times on returning to the home screen during testing

screen1-a1.deciding_evidence: the flag opened the course panel, which is what the language-flag convention promises

screen1-a2.glyph: grey flame outline with a numeral beside it
screen1-a2.description: flame outline with a count beside it in the top bar
screen1-a2.visible_text: none that names the purpose; flame glyph and the numeral "1"
screen1-a2.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "1 day streak" — told me to expect a streak page; not used in the verdict
screen1-a2.convention_relied_on: no established mobile convention: a flame is read as 'hot/trending' or 'fire', not as a daily-practice record — my reading, confidence medium
screen1-a2.initial_rationale: unlabeled glyph that is not a first-time-user convention; the bare numeral does not say what is being counted

test_cases.action: look for any caption or label on or near the flame, then tap it
test_cases.expected_result: no label appears; a page opens
test_cases.confirms_if: nothing on screen names it before the tap
test_cases.overturns_if: a label or caption appears on or next to it before the tap, or the glyph proves to follow a known convention
test_cases.observed_result: no caption or label near the flame at any point; tapping opened a full page titled 'Streak' with PERSONAL/FRIENDS tabs, a 'day streak!' count and a streak calendar

screen1-a2.deciding_evidence: nothing visible names the control before it is tapped; only the page it opens says 'Streak'
screen1-a2.recommendation: add a visible word under the glyph, e.g. 'Streak: 1 day', so the count and the destination are named
